w: Loch Eidhneach in Irish - lake of the place of ivy - Lough Inagh is a freshwater lake filling the Inagh Valley in Connemara, County Galway. The name recalls ivy once thick along its banks, one of the few details on record about this quiet valley lake before roads reached its shore.
s: A freshwater lake named for the ivy on its old shores
_facts: Irish name Loch Eidhneach means 'lake of the place of ivy'
Freshwater lake filling the Inagh Valley, Connemara, County Galway

w: Binn Leitri - Peak of the Wet Hillsides in Irish - Benlettery rises 557m as the southernmost of the Twelve Bens in Connemara National Park, County Galway, the 11th-tallest of the core Bens. The Ben Lettery An Oige youth hostel sits on its southern slopes, off the N59 road to Clifden.
s: Southernmost of the Twelve Bens, a hostel at its foot
_facts: Ben Lettery An Oige youth hostel on its southern slopes, off the N59 to Clifden

w: Built in 1754 on the edge of Ballynahinch Lake, this country house is overlooked by Benlettery in the Twelve Bens. Past owners include Richard Martin - 'Humanity Dick' - founder of the SPCA and MP for County Galway, and later the Maharaja Jam Sahib of Nawanagar, who bought the estate in 1924. Now a hotel.
s: A 1754 country house once owned by 'Humanity Dick' Martin
_facts: Built 1754, on the edge of Ballynahinch Lake and River
Owned by Richard Martin ('Humanity Dick'), SPCA founder and MP
Bought in 1924 by the Maharaja Jam Sahib of Nawanagar ('Ranji')

w: Maolchnoc - bald hill in Irish - Garraun stands 598m at the northern tip of the Twelve Bens/Garraun Complex, Connemara National Park, near Killary Harbour. Just short of the Vandeleur-Lynam height threshold, it still ranks as a Marilyn by prominence. Its slopes backdrop Kylemore Abbey and Kylemore Lough.
s: The peak that backdrops Kylemore Abbey
_facts: 598m, ranks as a Marilyn by prominence though just under Vandeleur-Lynam height
Southern slopes backdrop Kylemore Abbey and Kylemore Lough

w: Binn Doire Chlair - Derryclare Mountain rises 677m at the southern edge of the Twelve Bens, Connemara National Park, County Galway, the 5th-tallest of the core Bens. Derryclare Lough on its southern slopes is a classic Connemara scenic spot; Derryclare Wood on its eastern slopes holds a Statutory Nature Reserve.
s: 5th-tallest Ben, a lough and reserve at its feet
_facts: Derryclare Lough below it; Derryclare Wood is a Statutory Nature Reserve

w: Binn Braoin - Braon's Peak - Benbreen reaches 691m in the southern Twelve Bens, Connemara National Park, the 4th-tallest of the range after Benbaun, Bencorr and Bencollaghduff. Rather than a single summit, it presents as a high, narrow rocky ridge carrying several tops, unlike the classically peaked Bens around it.
s: A narrow rocky ridge, not a single peak
_facts: Profile described as a high narrow rocky ridge with several summits
